source: Anyone who spends time on the internet should not be surprised by lol ’s dominance.
claim: In 2019, lol (all case variants combined) accounts for 55.8% of laugh usage with 13,042,622 comments, ahead of haha at 14.8% (3,451,564) and lmao at 13.0% (3,033,063).

source: So many variables at play! In this next chart you can go deeper to see not only the market share of each laugh, but the ratio of lower to uppercase usage.
claim: Among the three most-used laughs, the lowercase form dominates: lol is 94.0% lowercase and 6.0% uppercase, haha is 98.9% lowercase and 1.1% uppercase, and lmao is 92.0% lowercase and 8.0% uppercase.
code: df.assign(laugh=df.id.str.lower(), case=np.where(df.id.str.islower(), 'lower', 'upper')).groupby(['laugh', 'case']).count_2019.sum().unstack().assign(total=lambda x: x.sum(axis=1)).sort_values('total', ascending=False).pipe(lambda x: x[['lower', 'upper']].div(x['total'], axis=0) * 100)

source: Here is the rise of lol in one chart.
claim: Among the top 20 laughs, lol's usage share rose from 29.2% in 2009 to 56.0% in 2018.
code: df[df.id.str.islower()].assign(laugh=lambda d: d.id.str.lower()).groupby('laugh')[[f'count_{y}' for y in range(2009, 2019)]].sum().sort_values('count_2009', ascending=False).head(20).pipe(lambda t: t.div(t.sum()) * 100)[['count_2009', 'count_2018']]
